question: Explain Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSP) and their applications in AI.
title: CSP: Sudoku Solves Itself
hook: What if your Sudoku could solve itself?
answer: CSP is defined by three parts: a set of variables X1..Xn, a domain D1..Dn of allowed values for each variable, and a set of constraints C restricting which value combinations are allowed
A solution is a complete assignment (every variable gets a value from its domain) that violates no constraint
Example, map colouring: regions are variables, {red, green, blue} is the domain, constraint = neighbouring regions must have different colours (WA=R, NT=G, SA=B, Q=R, NSW=G, V=R, T=R)
Solved by backtracking search combined with constraint propagation
Applications: scheduling, Sudoku, timetabling, resource allocation
Memory trick: V D C = Variables, Domains, Constraints
